chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 1 is selected as the sole viable flow chemistry design, with Candidate 2 disqualified due to critical pressure drop and length violations. Candidate 1 achieves a combined score of 0.707, driven by strong kinetics (0.850) and safety (0.850) scores, ensuring the electrophilic aromatic substitution proceeds with high selectivity under controlled conditions. The primary flow advantage is selectivity, achieved through enhanced laminar mixing (r_mix=0.125) which minimizes side reactions compared to batch. Candidate 2 was rejected because its pressure drop (62.7 bar) exceeds the pump limit (20 bar) and its length (171 m) exceeds bench limits, making it physically unimplementable. The user's balanced objective is met by Candidate 1's moderate productivity and high safety margin. The main remaining uncertainty is the exact conversion yield (0.62) which may require optimization of residence time or temperature. The first experiment should verify the selectivity improvement over batch at the predicted residence time of 18.8 minutes.
